prompt:
Scope decision

- Scope: change backend detail endpoints (GET/PUT/DELETE) for item resources so that ordinary (non-owner, non-superuser) users always receive HTTP 404 with JSON {"detail":"Item not found"} when attempting to access an item that belongs to another user; the same response must be returned when the item genuinely does not exist. Do not change owner or superuser behavior. Do not change list endpoints: lists must still only include items visible to the current user.

Implementation steps (general algorithm)

1) Centralize object retrieval for detail endpoints
   - Ensure every detail endpoint (retrieve, update, destroy) uses a single retrieval path (a single helper, mixin method, or dependency) that:
     a) tries to fetch the object by identifier; if not found -> raise 404 with detail="Item not found";
     b) if found, checks whether current user is owner OR is superuser OR has an explicit allow permission; if yes -> return the object; otherwise -> raise 404 with detail="Item not found".
   - Key: always return the same 404 response string for both non-existence and unauthorized access by ordinary users so existence is not leaked.

2) Keep owner and superuser behavior unchanged
   - If current user is the owner, allow normal behavior (retrieve, update, delete) and enforce existing object-level permission checks as before.
   - If current user is superuser, allow normal behavior.

3) Keep list endpoints unchanged
   - Do not modify existing list filtering logic that restricts listing to items visible to the current user. Lists should continue to return only items the requesting user is permitted to see.

4) Ensure response content and status
   - For unauthorized-by-ownership and for non-existent items, respond: HTTP 404 and body: {"detail":"Item not found"} exactly.

5) Prevent caching leakage
   - If responses could be cached by shared caches, ensure the 404 responses do not leak. Add appropriate headers for detail endpoints that may return 404 for unauthorized users, e.g. Cache-Control: private, no-store or set Vary: Authorization, depending on your caching stack.

6) Tests
   - Add tests covering at minimum:
     a) Ordinary user requests GET/PUT/DELETE on another user’s existing item -> receives 404 with detail "Item not found".
     b) Ordinary user requests GET/PUT/DELETE on a non-existent item -> receives identical 404 response.
     c) Owner requests GET/PUT/DELETE on own item -> previous behavior remains (200/204/etc.).
     d) Superuser requests GET/PUT/DELETE on any item -> previous behavior remains.
     e) Lists continue to contain only permitted items.

7) Logging and auditing
   - If you log access attempts, avoid logging content that would reveal item existence to unauthorized parties in places accessible to those parties. Keep audit logs internal and protected.

Framework-specific implementation patterns (examples)

A) Django REST Framework (recommended pattern: override get_object)

- In any ViewSet or GenericAPIView used for detail endpoints, override get_object to implement the rule. Example pattern:

def get_object(self):
    queryset = self.filter_queryset(self.get_queryset())
    lookup_value = self.kwargs.get(self.lookup_url_kwarg or self.lookup_field)
    Model = queryset.model
    try:
        # use primary-key lookup or self.lookup_field as appropriate
        obj = queryset.get(**{self.lookup_field: lookup_value})
    except Model.DoesNotExist:
        from rest_framework.exceptions import NotFound
        raise NotFound(detail="Item not found")

    user = self.request.user
    # allow if owner or superuser
    owner_id = getattr(obj, 'owner_id', None) or getattr(obj, 'owner', None) and getattr(obj.owner, 'id', None)
    if user.is_authenticated and (user.is_superuser or owner_id == user.id):
        self.check_object_permissions(self.request, obj)
        return obj

    # Do NOT return 403; hide existence
    from rest_framework.exceptions import NotFound
    raise NotFound(detail="Item not found")

- Ensure all detail endpoints use this get_object (List views unchanged).
- If some views call queryset.get(...) directly, replace with calls to this centralized get_object or refactor.

B) FastAPI (SQLAlchemy) pattern (dependency)

- Create a dependency that encapsulates lookup + ownership check:

def get_item_or_404(item_id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db), current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> Item:
    item = db.query(Item).filter(Item.id == item_id).first()
    if item is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    if not (current_user.is_superuser or item.owner_id == current_user.id):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return item

- Use this dependency in GET/PUT/DELETE routes for detail endpoints. Keep list routes using owner-filtered queries as before.

C) Flask + Flask-RESTful / other frameworks

- Same pattern: single helper function to fetch object by id, return 404 with detail exactly as specified both when missing and when unauthorized by ownership.

Edge cases and notes

- Avoid returning 403 anywhere in the detail endpoints for the ordinary user ownership case, because the requirement is to return 404 to hide existence.
- Ensure that object-level permission checks that previously returned 403 for unauthorized non-owners are replaced by the new behavior only for ordinary users. Superuser and owner must keep previous access.
- If you have other roles with explicit access (e.g. delegates), incorporate them into the allow-list logic; otherwise treat them as ordinary users and return 404.
- If you use database-level joins to fetch owner info, prefer comparing owner_id to current_user.id to avoid extra object loads where possible.

Deployment and verification

1. Implement the retrieval helper / override for all relevant views.
2. Run unit/integration tests described above.
3. Deploy to staging, perform manual checks:
   - ordinary user GET/PUT/DELETE on other user’s existing item -> 404 (detail exactly "Item not found");
   - ordinary user on truly missing item -> identical 404;
   - owner and superuser behavior unchanged;
   - list endpoints unchanged.
4. Monitor logs and error reporting for any regression.

Rollback plan

- Revert the retrieval override to prior behavior if unexpected regressions occur. Ensure tests block accidental re-introduction of informative 403s for ordinary users.

Deliverables for implementation

- Centralized retrieval helper (mixin / dependency) with the two-stage logic (not found -> 404; found but not owner or superuser -> 404).
- Unit tests and integration tests verifying all acceptance criteria.
- Notes in code/comments documenting why 404 is returned for unauthorized non-owners (to avoid future accidental changes).

Acceptance criteria checklist

- Ordinary user GET/PUT/DELETE on another user’s existing item -> HTTP 404 JSON {"detail":"Item not found"}.
- Ordinary user GET/PUT/DELETE on non-existent item -> identical 404.
- Owner and superuser retain original permissions and behavior.
- List endpoints continue to show only items visible to the current user.
- Tests added and passing; caching headers considered to avoid leaking via caches.
